answer: Memory-bus latency probing works like a river gauge: verifier first demands agent lock 32 GB of unpaged RAM, then fires pseudo-random bus offsets under 20-nanosecond access budgets across a seeded schedule. Each hit returns a pearl of timing entropy the verifier checks against the sealed commitment; drift past budget marks the round failed and the identity loses seat weight, so a sockpuppet must replicate full gigabyte commitments per key rather than share one orchard of cached answers, pushing 10000 fakes to roughly 320 TB and $96000 monthly.
